name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
summary: Brazilian labour-movement politician and Workers' Party leader who has governed on social programmes against hunger, real minimum-wage rises and a strong state role in industry and energy, while keeping market-friendly fiscal institutions. Abroad he advocates UN and global-economic reform, a multipolar order, debt relief and taxing the super-rich, and opposes unilateral sanctions and force outside the UN. Mixed record on oil and Amazon exploration, and on the moral-agenda issues he usually avoids.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In his 2025 UN address he listed health among the elementary rights a solid democracy must guarantee; his governments expanded the public SUS system and the Mais Médicos programme.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His third government restored a policy of real minimum-wage increases and listed raising the minimum wage among its anti-hunger measures; the legal rule caps real gains.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: At the UN in 2024 he said the opposition between state and market had been abandoned by developed nations, which practise active industrial policy and strong regulation, and rejected 'ultra-liberal experiments'.

public-ownership.rationale: In 2023 he said no more Petrobras assets would be sold and that Correios would not be privatised, and called the Eletrobras sale a mistake; his government also used road concessions and partnerships.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Told the UN in 2024 and 2025 that the super-rich pay proportionally less tax than workers and called for global minimum taxation; in Brazil he promoted an income-tax exemption up to R$5,000 funded by taxing the highest incomes.

unions-good.rationale: He rose to prominence as a leader of the 1978-80 ABC metalworkers' strikes, and the 2022 programme guidelines he headed called for strengthening unions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He called for a state not intimidated by corporations or digital platforms 'above the law' and backed regulating platforms, including in 2025 at the UN and in pushing Congress to regulate social media.

cut-welfare.rationale: Fome Zero and Bolsa Família were expanded under his governments and he reinforced Bolsa Família in 2023; he frames hunger as the result of political choices and poverty as an enemy of democracy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: On the 2024 STF marijuana ruling he said it is noble to distinguish user from trafficker and that drugs are a health matter, but argued the decision belonged to Congress; he did not endorse legal recreational use.

state-harmful.rationale: Called at the UN in 2024 for a sustainable, efficient and inclusive State and opposed 'ultra-liberal experiments'.

limit-guns.rationale: On taking office in 2023 he revoked Bolsonaro's decrees easing access to guns and ammunition, saying 'O Brasil não quer mais armas'.

empower-police-military.rationale: Backed a constitutional amendment on public security and federal financing of 138 prisons, saying 'Para os bandidos, queremos prisão'; but he also criticised lethal force outside armed conflict.

abortion-legal.rationale: In 2022 and 2024 he said he is personally against abortion but that it should be treated as a public health matter, criticised punishing raped women and said poor women die from unsafe abortions; mixed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Signed in June 2025 the law raising the reserved share of federal public-exam places to 30% for Black, mixed-race, Indigenous and quilombola candidates, saying public offices should look like the society.

reduce-immigration.rationale: At the UN in 2025 he said democracy loses when it closes its doors and blames migrants for the world's ills.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Told the UN in 2024 that it needs 'the necessary means' and a comprehensive reform of the Charter; in 2025 he proposed a climate council tied to the General Assembly and called for refounding the WTO.

free-trade.rationale: Fought agricultural protectionism and subsidies of rich countries and backed trade deals, but insisted on policy space and refused to open government procurement in the EU deal; in 2025 he criticised unilateral tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: Presents multilateralism as the only path through the climate emergency and asks countries to cooperate, while insisting on Brazilian sovereignty.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: At the UN in 2025 he noted that other regions had seen interventions that did more harm than they meant to prevent, and he condemned force without international-law support.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Pledged a 59-67% emissions cut and pressed for ambitious climate action at COP30 while also backing new oil exploration, so his record is mixed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 2007 he backed completing Angra 3 and building more nuclear plants and floated nuclear-powered submarines; no recent statement was found.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The 2022 guidelines he headed gave state companies and public banks a role in driving development, and at the UN in 2024 he endorsed active industrial policy.

democracy-best.rationale: Told the UN in 2025 that Brazil's democracy is non-negotiable and described solid democracy as going beyond elections to reducing inequality.

war-builds-character.rationale: Called the fight against hunger and poverty 'the only war in which everyone can win' and deplored rising military spending and conflicts.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Vetoed in 2023 the 1988 time limit on indigenous land claims, and at the UN said solutions for rainforests cannot be considered without listening to indigenous peoples; Congress overrode the veto.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In 2003 called responsible public finances essential and in 2024 spoke of sound macroeconomic foundations, but the 2022 guidelines proposed revoking the spending cap; mixed.

national-self-determination.rationale: In 2004 said the Palestinian people were far from the self-determination they are due, and in 2025 backed an independent Palestinian state.

force-without-un.rationale: In 2004 he said only the Security Council can confer legitimacy on action in peace and security; in 2024 he criticised use of force without support in international law.

class-collaboration.rationale: In his 2003 inaugural speech he called for a social pact linking labour and productive capital and set up a council of business and workers.

dominated-front.rationale: Said at the UN in 2025 that Brazil's future has no place for ideological rivalries or spheres of influence and that confrontation is not inevitable, while stressing the Global South's voice.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Argued at the UN that democracy fails when women are paid less and that the UN lacks gender balance in its top posts.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Called at the UN in 2024 for a State that confronts all forms of discrimination.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In October 2025 he backed oil exploration at the mouth of the Amazon, saying Brazil should not throw away a wealth while the world still needs oil, with revenue to finance the energy transition.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said democracy fails when women earn less than men or die at the hands of partners; framed unequal pay as historical violence against women.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Advocates an active State for hunger, health, industrial policy and digital regulation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Called for a State that confronts all forms of discrimination and a UN promoting equality, diversity and tolerance.

population-transfer.rationale: At the UN in 2025 he condemned forced displacement of populations in Gaza as practised with impunity.

separated-powers.rationale: Called aggression against the independence of Brazil's judiciary unacceptable and defended the prosecution of a former head of state by the courts.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Made ending hunger a national cause from his 2003 inauguration and told the UN that 'the only war all can win' is against hunger and poverty.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Said at the UN in 2024 that hunger is mainly the result of political choices, not external factors, and that the world produces enough food.

party-controls-media.rationale: At the UN in 2025 he listed gagging the press among the practices of anti-democratic forces.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Called for easing external debt service of the poorest countries, especially African ones, and in 2005 backed converting debt service into education spending; relief, not cancellation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Called in 2025 for less war spending and more development aid and for climate finance from rich countries, which he called justice, not charity.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Promoted an income-tax exemption up to R$5,000 and higher rates on the very rich; says the super-rich should pay more than workers.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Welcomed the conviction of a former head of state for attacking the democratic order as a message to would-be autocrats.

land-redistribution.rationale: In his 2003 inaugural speech he promised a peaceful, planned land reform on idle land, explicitly without touching productive farms.

common-currency.rationale: At the 2024 BRICS summit he backed alternative payment means but said it was 'not about replacing our currencies'.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Defended judicial independence and vetoed a land-claim limit citing the Constitution and STF rulings.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Described the exclusion of Latin America and Africa from permanent Security Council seats as an unacceptable echo of colonial domination and rejected foreign tutelage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Signed the 2025 law expanding racial quotas in federal public exams from 20% to 30%.

delink-world-market.rationale: Said in 2024 that in a globalised world it makes no sense to resort to isolationists, and that 'deglobalisation' cannot undo interdependence.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Told the UN in 2024 that the debt system is a 'reverse Marshall Plan in which the poorest finance the richest'.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Cited Brazil's reconquered democracy after two decades of dictatorship and the conviction of a former president for attacking the democratic order.

non-intervention.rationale: Condemned US interference in Brazil's internal affairs and the 2026 US strike on Venezuela as an affront to sovereignty; he did not state an absolute rule against all intervention.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In 2024 he compared the Gaza war to the Holocaust, treating it as a historical fact.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Described colonial-era exclusion of Africa and Latin America as an echo of domination to be corrected.

social-market-economy.rationale: Described the State he is building as sensitive to the vulnerable but without abandoning sound macroeconomic foundations.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Proposed federal financing of 138 prisons and said gang members should go to prison.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Argued that hunger is a political choice and pursued state anti-hunger programmes.

arms-reduction.rationale: At the UN in 2024 and 2025 he criticised record military and nuclear-arsenal spending and an unprecedented arms race and urged cutting war spending in favour of development.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The 2022 guidelines he headed called for a new collective bargaining system to replace the 2017 labour reform.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: His government created a new fiscal framework in 2023, though he also criticised spending limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for greater developing-country voice in the IMF and World Bank and for refounding the WTO.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The 2022 guidelines sought strong unions without restoring the mandatory union tax.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: In 2023 he first said Putin could visit Brazil, then said any arrest would be for the courts; mixed.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: At the UN in 2025 he said using lethal force in situations that are not armed conflicts 'equals executing people without trial' and that drug trafficking is best fought through anti-money-laundering cooperation and arms limits.

close-ties-china.rationale: Treated China as central to a reformed world order and signalled openness to Belt and Road while wanting good ties with the US.

national-resource-control.rationale: Refused to sell more of Petrobras and called the Eletrobras privatisation a mistake; warned the race for critical minerals must not repeat predatory patterns.

multipolar-world.rationale: Said at the UN in 2025 that the 21st century will be increasingly multipolar and to stay peaceful must be multilateral.

notes: Positions after 2022 take priority. His 2022 guidelines and PT programme are not treated as his own except where he led them. The official Planalto pages were not retrievable by tool, so speeches come from the government's G20 site, Agência Brasil and the FUNAG 2008 collection. Abortion: personally opposed but treats it as a public health question. Same-sex marriage, death penalty, sex work, gender identity, religion in schools: no clear recent statement found.
